assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology, from proglucagon-derived peptide biology and the incretin effect to receptor agonists that treat type 2 diabetes and obesity, is a clear discovery-to-therapy arc with a pronounced change in clinical practice and in how metabolic disease is understood.
assessment.attribution: Drucker and Holst established GLP-1 biology and its physiological actions; Mojsov's work on the active peptide form is credited but contested in priority. Knudsen is a pivotal industrial developer of the long-acting analogues, which is arguably a different kind of contribution. The three-person configuration leaves out other early contributors, including Habener, if the credited strings were extended, and I cannot verify the priority claims.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism and benefit are replicated across many large trials, with decades of follow-up. Recognition is timely and the impact is now broad across cardiometabolic disease.
uncertainties: Priority dispute around the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide and its early characterization.
Whether the prize should reward basic physiology, the drug development, or both is unresolved.
Long-term safety and broader indications are still emerging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new principle of intracellular signaling from the ER to the nucleus, with an elegant set of mechanisms (IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing, ATF6, PERK) and lasting relevance to secretory-cell physiology, diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter independently and complementarily elucidated the pathway in yeast and mammals, which supports a compact and fair two-person prize. Some other contributors (for example Kaufman, Ron) exist in the wider literature, but I rely on the supplied credited names only.
assessment.maturity: The field is thoroughly confirmed and mature, with decades of independent work. Timing is not premature.
uncertainties: Therapeutic translation is still limited, so the case rests on fundamental cell biology.
Exact division of credit between yeast and mammalian work and other contributors is only partly known to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology a transformative method for causal control of defined cell populations, built on microbial rhodopsin channels. It changed experimental practice across the field and underpins early clinical vision-restoration efforts.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across at least six people with distinct roles: channelrhodopsin identification and characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg), the neuronal demonstration (Boyden, Deisseroth) and earlier genetically targeted photostimulation ideas (Miesenböck). A three-person limit forces difficult choices, and my selection is provisional.
assessment.maturity: The method is widely validated and in near-universal use, so it is mature. Therapeutic applications are early.
uncertainties: The allocation among the six credited names is highly contested.
The prize may be argued to recognize a tool rather than a discovery about disease or physiology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered CAR-T cells produce durable remissions in otherwise refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new class of living therapeutics, with clear and lasting clinical and scientific impact.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain led the design and clinical proof for CD19 CARs, with costimulatory-domain engineering central. Rosenberg contributed foundational adoptive cell therapy and early gene-engineered T-cell trials, though his role is distinct from CAR design. The original CAR concept (Eshhar and others) is outside the supplied names, so I cannot confirm it can be recognized.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and several years of follow-up confirm efficacy, but long-term safety and extension to solid tumors remain open. Recognition is reasonable now.
uncertainties: The credited list omits the originators of the chimeric receptor concept.
Limited success in solid tumors and toxicity concerns.
Fair split between engineering and adoptive cell therapy lineages.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeting BCR-ABL with imatinib turned chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease into a manageable one, and proved the principle of molecularly targeted cancer therapy. The effect on the field and on patients is substantial and unambiguous.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound development), Druker (clinical translation) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) form a coherent trio. The earlier cytogenetic and oncogene discoveries behind BCR-ABL are not part of the credited names, which may weigh against a prize for the therapy alone.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of clinical follow-up confirm durable outcomes. Highly mature, and the recognition is arguably late but not premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views the earlier BCR-ABL discoveries as a necessary part of the prize.
Relative weight of the industrial contribution compared with clinical translation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Chaperonin-assisted folding showed that proteins in cells often need an assisted, ATP-dependent folding cage (GroEL/GroES, TRiC) to reach the native state, which reshaped protein biochemistry and our understanding of proteostasis and misfolding disease.
assessment.attribution: Horwich and Hartl made the decisive experimental demonstration in mitochondria and in vitro, which supports a clean two-person configuration. Related earlier chaperone work, such as heat-shock and Hsp70 or the Ellis chaperone concept, is outside the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed through structural and biochemical studies over thirty years. Mature.
uncertainties: The link to human disease is indirect, and the prize category may favor more medical impact.
Priority relative to other chaperone discoveries is not resolved by the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR and mTOR signaling is a central regulator of cell growth, metabolism and ageing, with extensive consequences for cancer, immunosuppression and metabolic disease, and rapamycin-derived drugs in clinical use.
assessment.attribution: Hall's identification of TOR in yeast is the foundational discovery. Schreiber's FKBP12-rapamycin work supplied the chemical biology link to the target. Sabatini's identification of mTOR and the mTORC1 pathway is important but I leave him out of this configuration because the three-name limit forces a choice and credit among many contributors is complex.
assessment.maturity: Highly confirmed and extended by many labs. Mature, with ongoing clinical expansion.
uncertainties: Attribution among Hall, Sabatini, Schreiber and others (for example Sabers, Brown, Heitman) is not clear.
Sabatini's inclusion versus exclusion is a judgment call that I cannot resolve from the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Notch signaling is a conserved mechanism for local cell-fate decisions, with major relevance to development, stem-cell maintenance, T-cell development and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Artavanis-Tsakonas, Greenwald and Struhl each made decisive genetic and molecular contributions in Drosophila and C. elegans, but the credit is shared with other major contributors in the field, and a three-person limit is difficult.
assessment.maturity: The pathway is robust and well confirmed, and clinical consequences are partial (gamma-secretase inhibitors, Notch in leukemia). Recognition is timely, with the disease link still developing.
uncertainties: Overlap with many other important contributors to the pathway.
Direct medical translation is limited so far.
